spots.name: Aker Stadion
spots.label: Aker Stadion

text.directions_text: Start from Molde town centre and head west towards Reknes on the fjord shore; the stadium is the large building by the water. There is no public transport stop listed for this spot, but the stadium can be reached on foot from the town centre. The phone icon on the map is about 230 m east of the subject. The Navigate buttons below take you straight there.
text.geographic_location: Aker Stadion is at Reknes, on the shore of the Moldefjord, just west of Molde town centre.
text.description: Aker Stadion is the home ground of Molde football club, and it sits right on the edge of the Moldefjord at Reknes, just west of the town centre. It is a big, clean-lined building. The outside is clad in two colours of granite, with glass and aluminium, so it gives a strong shape against the water and sky. It was designed by the architect Kjell Kosberg and opened on 18 April 1998. A year later it won the City Prize, a Norwegian award for building projects that improve the surrounding area. Locals sometimes call it "Røkkeløkka", after the businessman who paid for most of it. It holds a little over 11,000 spectators, so the structure is large but not overwhelming, and it fits into a phone frame well from a short distance away. The phone icon on the map is about 230 m east of the subject. That distance is useful because you can fit the whole building in one shot without tilting the phone upwards. Look for the long granite and glass walls, the roofline and any clear sky above. If the fjord is visible beside the stadium, include a slice of water to give the picture a sense of place.
text.access_note: The stadium can be photographed from outside in the open; for matches, tours or going inside, check the official site before you go.

shooting_on_your_phone.where_to_stand: Stand about 230 m east of the subject, at the phone icon on the map, and face west. From here the stadium sits in the middle of the view with room around it.
shooting_on_your_phone.how_to_frame: Turn on gridlines and place the stadium on one of the lower thirds, with sky above. Keep the phone level so the long horizontal lines of the building stay straight. If you can see the fjord, include a strip of water at the edge of the frame. For a tighter second picture, zoom in on the granite and glass of the facade.
shooting_on_your_phone.phone_settings_tip: Tap on the stadium to set focus, then drag the exposure slider down slightly if the sky is bright, so the building keeps its colour. Check that the picture is straight before you take it.
shooting_on_your_phone.best_time: Choose a dry day with some light on the front of the stadium. Evening light can look warm, but check which way the building faces the sun before you commit to one spot.
shooting_on_your_phone.phone_lens: Start with the default lens (1x), which fits the whole stadium from this distance. Try telephoto (2x or more) for a tighter shot of the facade and roofline.

spots.alt: Aker Stadion, Molde: the home ground of Molde football club. Photo spot

text.directions_text: No station or tram stop is listed for this spot, so check a local map or transport planner for the route. The phone icon on the map is about 65 m east of the subject. The Navigate buttons below take you straight there.
text.geographic_location: Varden is a viewpoint in Molde.
text.description:
Varden is a viewpoint in Molde, and the third stop on this map. It is a place to slow down and take in the view rather than a single building or monument to point at. That suits a phone well. A wide scene with layers of land, water and sky is easy to capture, and there is usually time to try a few versions.

The phone icon on the map is about 65 m east of the subject. From there you look west towards it. Stand with the marker in front of you and keep some of the surroundings in the frame, so the picture shows where you are and not only the spot itself.

Start with the default lens (1x) and turn on the gridlines so the horizon stays level. Then switch to ultra-wide (0.5x) for a broader view, and try a zoom (2x or more, depending on your phone) to pick out a single detail in the distance. Tap the screen on the part of the scene you care about most, then drag the exposure slider down slightly if the sky looks too bright. Take a few frames, as the view and the light can change within minutes. Clean the lens with a soft cloth first, because a smudge shows up as haze in wide views.
text.access_note: Access rules for this viewpoint are not confirmed here, so check the official site before you go.

shooting_on_your_phone.where_to_stand: Stand about 65 m east of the subject, at the phone icon on the map, and face west.
shooting_on_your_phone.how_to_frame: Switch on the gridlines and put the horizon on the upper or lower line, depending on whether the land or the sky matters more. Keep a little foreground at the edge of the frame to give a sense of depth.
shooting_on_your_phone.phone_settings_tip: Tap to focus on the middle distance and lower the exposure slider a touch if the sky is bright. Try panorama for a sweeping view, moving slowly and keeping the phone level.
shooting_on_your_phone.best_time: Soft light early or late in the day usually flatters a wide view, and a clear day shows the most distance.
shooting_on_your_phone.phone_lens: Start with the default lens (1x). Use ultra-wide (0.5x) for the full scene and a 2x-5x zoom, depending on your phone, for distant details.

text.directions_text: No tram or train stops are listed for this spot, so start from Molde town centre and head for the city square, Gørvellplassen. The Navigate buttons below take you to the subject.
text.geographic_location: Teatret Vårt is in the centre of Molde, in the Plassen building on the city square, Gørvellplassen.
text.description:
Teatret Vårt is the regional theatre for Møre og Romsdal county. It was established in 1972 and is based in Molde. It also works with the annual Molde International Jazz Festival. The theatre is housed in the Plassen building, a large granite structure that fills the city square. Its architect describes it as literally gripping the square, and that is what makes it a good subject for a phone photo. The stone mass, the broad staircase and the stepped seating rising towards the roof give you strong shapes and lines, even on a quiet day.

The best view is from the square itself, Gørvellplassen, where you can see the building's full form from the front. If you want something different, walk to the foot of the building, at Plassen. From there you can photograph the wide stone staircase and the facade, with the seating stepping up towards the roof.

Keep your phone level so the long edges of the building stay straight. Use the gridlines to help, and leave a little space around the building so it sits in the square rather than filling the whole frame. Add a person on the steps or in the square if you want to show the scale.
text.access_note: The square is an open public space, but check the official site before you go if you want to use the staircase, go inside or go up to the roof.

shooting_on_your_phone.where_to_stand: Stand in Gørvellplassen. The granite Plassen building filling the city square, which is the main frontal view of the theatre's home. From here the Plassen building fills the square in front of you and you see the main frontal view of the theatre's home, with the theatre just to the north.
shooting_on_your_phone.how_to_frame: Turn on the gridlines and line up the building's horizontal edges with them. Keep the phone level and at chest height to avoid leaning verticals. Include a bit of the square in the foreground to show how the building grips it. As an alternative, go to the foot of the building at Plassen and photograph the broad stone staircase and facade, with the stepped seating rising towards the roof.
shooting_on_your_phone.phone_settings_tip: Tap on the facade to set focus, then drag the exposure slider down slightly if the pale stone or sky looks washed out. Check the edges of the ultra-wide shot, as buildings can stretch near the corners.
shooting_on_your_phone.best_time: Soft daylight usually suits the stone best. At dusk, try night mode with your phone resting against something steady.
shooting_on_your_phone.phone_lens: Start with the ultra-wide (0.5x) to fit the whole granite building and some of the square into one frame. Switch to the default lens (1x) for a more natural view of the facade. A telephoto/zoom (2x-5x, depending on your phone) is useful for details of the stonework and the stepped seating.
